summary: Charles Bally was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1886-1889) and under Ferdinand de Saussure (c. 1893-1913). He held a post at the University of Geneva from around 1893 to 1939.

Charles Barbier de Meynard worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Jules Mohl, he held posts at École des langues orientales, Institut de France, and Collège de France.

Charles Burnett is a historian and philosopher who earned his BA and doctorate at the University of Cambridge. He held positions at St John's College, the University of Sheffield, and notably the Warburg Institute, where he became professor in 1999.

Charles Cutler Torrey worked in religious studies and history/archaeology, studying under Theodor Nöldeke. He taught Semitic languages at Andover Theological Seminary (1892-1900), served as professor at Yale University (1900-1932), and founded the American Schools of Oriental Research.

Charles D. Orzech is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology who earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago. He chaired Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro (attested 1998-2006) and was a fellow at the National Humanities Center.

Charles Duroiselle worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He taught Pali at the University of Rangoon, collaborated with the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, and served as Superintendent of the Archaeological Survey of Burma from 1912 to 1940.

Charles Edmund Godakumbura was an Indologist and historian who earned multiple degrees at the University of London. He taught at University College, Colombo and SOAS, and served as Commissioner of Archaeology for the Archaeological Survey of India (1956-1967).

Charles Eliot was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology who studied at Balliol College, Oxford. He served in the Foreign Office, held a post at the University of Sheffield, and was principal of The University of Hong Kong.

Charles Elliott was active in Indology and history/archaeology. He served in the East India Company from around 1795 to 1827 and was Treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from circa 1836 to 1856.

Charles Gabriel Seligman studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital. Working in history and archaeology, he held the chair of Ethnology at the London School of Economics and the University of London from 1913 to 1934.

Charles Goodman is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Allan Gibbard. He is an associate professor at Binghamton University (attested 2013).
Charles H. Long was a religious studies scholar who earned his BD and PhD at the University of Chicago. He held faculty posts at Chicago, UNC Chapel Hill, Duke, Syracuse, and UC Santa Barbara.

Charles Hallisey is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Colgate, Harvard, University of Pennsylvania, and University of Chicago. He has held faculty appointments at Loyola University Chicago, Harvard University, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Charles Henry Tawney was an Indologist educated at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as professor and principal at Presidency College, Chennai, headed Presidency University, and later served as librarian of the India Office Library from 1892 to 1903.

Charles Malamoud is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris. He held posts at the University of Lyon (c. 1957-1972) and as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (c. 1979-1998).
Charles Oman was a historian who studied at New College, Oxford from around 1878 to 1882. He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Oxford from circa 1883 until 1946.

Charles Otto Blagden was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He was educated at Dulwich College and Corpus Christi College, Oxford, and later held a post at SOAS University of London from around 1917 to 1935.

Charles Philip Brown was an Indologist and linguist educated at East India Company College. After serving in the Indian Civil Service from 1817 to 1854, he became Professor of Telugu at the University of London from circa 1865 to 1879.

Charles Ramble is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Durham University and under Michael Aris. He held academic posts at the University of Oxford, Wolfson College, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Charles Rieu was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian studies who studied at Geneva and Bonn under Christian Lassen. He served as Curator of Oriental Manuscripts at the British Museum and Adams Professor of Arabic at Cambridge.
